extracted.intended_audience: instructors and students in academic communications/journalism/public relations courses
extracted.subtask_description: A classroom grading rubric for student press-release writing assignments that specifies weighted evaluation criteria (structure, clarity, content, grammar, tone, distribution) and a five-level rating scale; also offers an alternate implicit 1–5-per-item scoring checklist summing to 40 points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure and Format (20%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adherence to standard press release structure: Headline; Dateline; Introduction (lead); Body; Boilerplate; Contact information; '###' or '-30-' end marker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weighted at 20% of the grade. Check for presence and correct ordering of standard elements, proper dateline formatting, inclusion of boilerplate and contact info, and an appropriate end marker.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity (20%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear, concise communication; reader can understand without ambiguity; effective transmission of necessary information; free from confusing language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weighted at 20% of the grade. Evaluate sentence and paragraph-level clarity, concision, logical flow, and whether key facts are presented unambiguously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content (25%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevant information; accurate facts; engaging to reader; newsworthy; all 5Ws + H addressed; appropriate quotes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weighted at 25% of the grade. Assess completeness (who/what/when/where/why/how), factual accuracy, relevance and news value, and the appropriateness and attribution of quoted material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grammar and Spelling (15%)
rubrics_metrics.description: No spelling errors; correct grammar; proper punctuation; AP style adherence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weighted at 15% of the grade. Check for mechanical correctness, consistency with AP style (as specified), and absence of typos or grammatical mistakes that impede understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and Voice (10%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Third person; active voice; journalistic (not promotional); audience-appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weighted at 10% of the grade. Evaluate whether the release uses a professional journalistic tone, avoids overt promotion, maintains appropriate voice and perspective for the intended audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution Strategy (10%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Target audience identified; distribution plan articulated; timing rationale; outlet selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weighted at 10% of the grade. Assess whether the student has identified appropriate targets, justified timing and channels, and selected suitable outlets for the release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five-Level Rating Scale (5 = Exemplary to 1 = Beginning)
rubrics_metrics.description: 5 - Exemplary: All criteria met excellently; publication-ready; no edits needed; distinctive and compelling. 4 - Proficient: Most criteria met well; minor edits needed; clear and effective. 3 - Adequate: Basic criteria met; some revision needed; functional. 2 - Developing: Several criteria not met; significant revision needed. 1 - Beginning: Most criteria not met; major revision required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this descriptive scale to assign holistic performance levels per criterion or overall. The rubric pairs the weighted criteria with these level descriptors to determine final grades.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit: Format adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Format adherence (listed as an implicit checklist item).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of an alternate checklist where each item is scored 1–5. Overlaps with 'Structure and Format' above; in the implicit checklist it contributes to a total out of 40 points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit: Clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity (listed as an implicit checklist item).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the 1–5 implicit scoring checklist; overlaps with the explicit 'Clarity' criterion. Score for how clear and understandable the release is.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit: Content quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Content quality (listed as an implicit checklist item).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the 1–5 implicit scoring checklist; overlaps with 'Content'. Score for relevance, accuracy, newsworthiness, and completeness of facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit: Grammar/spelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Grammar/spelling (listed as an implicit checklist item).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the 1–5 implicit scoring checklist; overlaps with the explicit 'Grammar and Spelling' criterion. Score mechanical correctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit: Tone appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Tone appropriate (listed as an implicit checklist item).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the 1–5 implicit scoring checklist; overlaps with 'Tone and Voice'. Score appropriateness of voice and promotional vs. journalistic tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit: News value
rubrics_metrics.description: News value (listed as an implicit checklist item).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the 1–5 implicit scoring checklist; this specifically foregrounds 'newsworthy' as an independently scored item, even though it's also included under 'Content'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit: Quote quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Quote quality (listed as an implicit checklist item).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the 1–5 implicit scoring checklist; evaluates whether quotes are appropriate, attributed, and add value to the release (overlaps with 'Content').

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit: Audience targeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Audience targeting (listed as an implicit checklist item).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the 1–5 implicit scoring checklist; overlaps with 'Distribution Strategy'. In the implicit scheme, score each item 1–5 and sum for a total out of 40 points.
